    Inflating a corank-one nonnegative form to a graph form #

    Rad1 q y: q is nonnegative, y ≫ 0 is a radical vector, and q vanishes only on rational multiples of y. Inflations preserve this, with y ↦ y + y_b e_a (Rad1.inflate). Since the off-diagonal coefficients of a nonnegative form lie in [-2, 2], only finitely many forms occur, and the radical vector strictly grows; so repeated inflation ends at a form with no coefficient +1 (exists_terminal).
